metadata.notes: Updated: Agent isolation via bare clone + git worktrees from Phase 1. Agents work in D:\bots\worker-N, NEVER in the user's working copy. Three phases: Bootstrap (get one issue working), Loop (continuous operation), Scale (multi-session). Batch refs P01-P14.

issues._phase: Phase 1: Bootstrap — Get One Issue Working
issues.title: Research CC headless invocation for agentic project work (extends #157)

sections.summary: Determine the best method to invoke Claude Code programmatically from a script, passing a Samverk issue as the task, and letting CC work autonomously in a project directory.
sections.context:
This extends the existing #157 (Claude Code Remote Control spike). The current CT 202 agents use `claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions` which is one-shot: send prompt, get text response. This works for simple EDIT block generation but CC can't iterate, run tests, or use its full agentic toolset.

For the PC agent, CC needs to run in an isolated worktree directory (NOT the user's working copy) with full capabilities. Research these invocation modes:

1. `claude --print -p 'prompt'` — one-shot, current approach, limited
2. `claude` with stdin piping — does CC accept a task via stdin in non-interactive mode?
3. `claude --task 'description'` — does a task/headless mode exist?
4. `claude` launched in a directory with a crafted .claude/task file or equivalent
5. CC SDK or API — is there a programmatic interface beyond the CLI?
6. `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` without `--print` — does this enter full agentic mode headlessly?

Key requirements:
- CC must have full file system access in the worktree directory
- CC must be able to run terminal commands (go test, go build, git)
- CC must work headlessly (no human interaction during execution)
- CC must terminate when the task is complete (not hang waiting for input)
- Exit code or output must indicate success/failure
- Must work on Windows (PowerShell invocation)

Also research: How does CC handle CLAUDE.md? If CC is launched in a worktree directory that contains CLAUDE.md (inherited from the repo), does it read it automatically? This would give CC full project context without prompt injection.

Additionally: does CC handle git worktree directories correctly? Some tools get confused by .git files (pointer to the shared bare repo) vs .git directories. Verify CC works in a worktree.
acceptance_criteria: Each invocation mode tested on Windows with a trivial task
Best mode identified with rationale (capability vs reliability vs complexity)
Document: how to pass the task description, how CC finds project context, how it terminates
Document: what CC can and cannot do in headless mode (file access, terminal, git, web)
Document: CLAUDE.md auto-loading behavior
Document: exit code semantics and output parsing
Document: any limitations or gotchas on Windows specifically
Confirmed: CC works correctly in a git worktree directory (not just a normal clone)
Findings posted as issue comment with recommendation

issues._phase: Phase 1: Bootstrap — Get One Issue Working
issues.title: Set up agent workspace infrastructure (bare clone + worktree scripts)

sections.summary: Create the agent workspace infrastructure: a bare clone of the repo that agents create worktrees from, completely isolated from the user's working copy.
sections.context:
Agents must NEVER touch the user's working copy at D:\devspace\Samverk. Instead:

```
D:\devspace\Samverk\                ← USER's copy. Read by user. Never touched by agents.
D:\bots\         ← Agent workspace root
├── samverk.git\                    ← Bare clone (shared object store)
├── worker-1\                       ← Worktree: agent session 1's working directory
├── worker-2\                       ← Worktree: agent session 2's working directory
└── worker-3\                       ← Worktree: agent session 3's working directory
```

The bare clone is created once:
```powershell
git clone --bare https://github.com/HerbHall/samverk.git D:\bots\samverk.git
```

Worktrees are created per-session and destroyed after:
```powershell
# Create worktree on a new branch
git -C D:\bots\samverk.git worktree add `
    D:\bots\worker-1 -b fix/42-add-feature main

# Agent works in D:\bots\worker-1
# Full repo content, own branch, own index, own working files

# Cleanup after task
git -C D:\bots\samverk.git worktree remove worker-1
```

Benefits:
- User's repo is completely untouched (different .git, different files)
- Worktrees share the object store (fast creation, ~0 disk overhead)
- Each worktree has its own branch and working state
- Multiple agents can work simultaneously without conflicts
- CLAUDE.md, Makefile, go.mod all present in each worktree (inherited from repo)

Build as PowerShell module: scripts/pc-agent/workspace.psm1

```powershell
function Initialize-AgentWorkspace {   # one-time bare clone setup
function New-AgentWorktree {           # create worktree for a task
function Remove-AgentWorktree {        # cleanup after task
function Update-BareRepo {             # git fetch to keep bare clone current
function Get-AvailableWorkerSlot {     # find next available worker-N name
function Test-WorktreeHealth {         # verify worktree is clean and functional
```

Config in .samverk/pc-agent.yaml:
```yaml
workspace:
  root: D:\bots
  bare_repo: samverk.git
  max_worktrees: 3
  remotes:
    github: https://github.com/HerbHall/samverk.git
    gitea: http://gitea.herbhall.net/samverk/samverk.git
```
acceptance_criteria: Bare clone created at configured location
New-AgentWorktree creates a functional working directory with correct branch
Worktree contains CLAUDE.md, Makefile, go.mod, full project structure
CC can be invoked in the worktree directory (verified manually)
Remove-AgentWorktree cleans up completely (no dangling refs)
Update-BareRepo fetches latest from configured remotes
Multiple worktrees can coexist (worker-1, worker-2, worker-3)
Get-AvailableWorkerSlot returns next free slot
Test-WorktreeHealth verifies git status is clean
User's D:\devspace\Samverk is never accessed by any function

issues._phase: Phase 1: Bootstrap — Get One Issue Working
issues.title: Design PC agent runner architecture and issue-to-prompt formatter

sections.summary: Design the PC agent runner: how it polls for work, provisions a worktree, formats issues into CC prompts, launches CC, and handles results. Write a design doc.
sections.context:
Based on P01 research findings, design the runner. The workspace infrastructure from P02 provides the isolation layer. Key components:

**Forge Poller:**
- Queries GitHub/Gitea for issues with status:queued + appropriate agent labels
- Filters by complexity label against autonomy tier config
- Claims issue by updating labels (status:queued → status:claimed, add assignee)
- Returns structured issue data

**Workspace Manager:**
- Calls Update-BareRepo to fetch latest code
- Calls New-AgentWorktree to provision an isolated working directory
- Worktree is on a branch named fix/<issue-number>-<slug>
- After task: Remove-AgentWorktree cleans up

**Prompt Formatter:**
- Takes a Samverk issue (YAML frontmatter + markdown sections)
- Generates a CC-consumable prompt
- Includes: issue body, acceptance criteria, project context hints
- References CLAUDE.md (present in worktree, CC reads automatically)
- Tells CC to run `make ci` before committing
- Tells CC to commit and push when done

**CC Launcher:**
- Starts CC in the WORKTREE directory (not user's repo)
- Passes the formatted prompt using the mode from P01
- Sets timeout based on estimated_tokens or complexity label
- Monitors process for completion
- Captures exit code and output

**Post-Task Handler:**
- Checks git status in the worktree
- If changes on a branch: push, open PR via forge API
- Update issue: add comment with results, change labels
- If failure: update issue with error, re-queue or escalate
- Cleanup: remove worktree

**Autonomy Gate:**
- Before launching CC, check the issue's autonomy tier
- Tier 1 (complexity:local): auto-proceed
- Tier 2 (complexity:cloud): auto-proceed but log prominently
- Tier 3 (complexity:ambiguous + priority:critical): skip, leave queued

Output: docs/pc-agent-design.md covering all components with sequence diagram.

CRITICAL INVARIANT: No component may read from or write to the user's working copy. All agent file operations happen in worktree directories under the workspace root.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc covers all six components (poller, workspace, formatter, launcher, post-task, autonomy gate)
Sequence diagram shows the full issue lifecycle including worktree create/destroy
Isolation invariant explicitly documented: agents never touch user's repo
CC invocation mode specified based on P01 findings
Prompt format documented with examples
Autonomy tier mapping documented
Error handling and retry strategy documented
Windows-specific considerations noted (paths, shell, process management)

issues._phase: Phase 1: Bootstrap — Get One Issue Working
issues.title: Build CC session launcher with worktree lifecycle (PowerShell)

sections.summary: Build the CC launcher that provisions a worktree, formats a Samverk issue into a CC prompt, runs CC headlessly in the isolated worktree, and cleans up.
sections.context:
Two sub-components:

**Prompt Formatter** (scripts/pc-agent/formatter.psm1):
Takes issue data (from forge poller) and produces the CC invocation. The prompt should:
- State the issue number and title
- Include the full issue body (frontmatter + sections)
- Remind CC to read CLAUDE.md (already present in worktree)
- Tell CC to run `make ci` before committing
- Tell CC to commit with a conventional commit message referencing the issue
- Tell CC to push the branch to origin
- Tell CC to signal completion (specific output or exit)

**CC Launcher** (scripts/pc-agent/launcher.psm1):
- Calls Update-BareRepo to fetch latest from remotes
- Calls New-AgentWorktree to create isolated working directory
- Worktree is on branch: fix/<issue-number>-<slug> based off latest main
- Sets working directory to the NEW WORKTREE (never the user's repo)
- Invokes CC with the formatted prompt using the mode from P01
- Sets a timeout (default: 15 minutes for cloud, 5 for local)
- Captures stdout/stderr and exit code
- Returns structured result: {Success, Output, Duration, Branch, WorktreePath, ExitCode}
- On completion (success or failure): worktree is NOT cleaned up yet (post-task handler does that)

The launcher must handle:
- CC hanging (timeout kill, then cleanup worktree)
- CC crashing (non-zero exit, preserve worktree for debugging if configured)
- CC succeeding but making no changes (nothing to commit)
acceptance_criteria: Worktree created from bare clone with correct branch name
Prompt formatter produces clear, structured prompt from issue data
CC is invoked in the WORKTREE directory (never the user's repo)
User's D:\devspace\Samverk is never accessed
Timeout kills CC process if exceeded
Exit code and output captured for post-task processing
Handles: success with changes, success with no changes, failure, timeout
Worktree path returned in result for post-task handler
Manual test: format a real issue, launch CC in worktree, verify isolation

issues._phase: Phase 1: Bootstrap — Get One Issue Working
issues.title: Build post-task handler: git push → PR → issue update → worktree cleanup (PowerShell)

sections.summary: Build the post-task handler that processes CC's output in the worktree: pushes changes, opens a PR, updates the issue, and cleans up the worktree.
sections.context:
After CC completes in the worktree, the handler:

1. **Check git status** in the worktree
   - If changes committed and pushed by CC: verify the branch exists on remote
   - If changes committed but not pushed: push the branch from the worktree
   - If changes staged but not committed: commit with auto-generated message, push
   - If no changes: mark issue as needs-qc with a comment explaining no changes were made

2. **Open PR** (if changes exist)
   - Title: conventional commit format referencing issue
   - Body: 'Closes #N' + summary from CC output
   - Head: work branch, Base: main
   - Add labels: status:needs-qc
   - Use forge poller's Open-PullRequest function

3. **Update issue**
   - Remove status:claimed, add status:needs-qc
   - Add comment: 'PC agent completed. PR #X opened. Duration: Nm Ns. Worker: worker-1.'
   - If failed: add comment with error, increment failure count, re-queue or escalate

4. **Cleanup worktree**
   - Call Remove-AgentWorktree to destroy the working directory
   - If preserve_on_failure is configured AND task failed: skip cleanup, log path for debugging
   - Delete the local branch from the bare repo after worktree removal

Location: scripts/pc-agent/post-task.psm1
acceptance_criteria: Detects CC's git changes correctly in the worktree
Pushes branch from worktree if CC committed but didn't push
Opens PR with correct title, body, and labels
Updates issue labels through full lifecycle transition
Failure handling: re-queues on first failure, escalates after max failures
Worktree removed after successful completion
Worktree preserved on failure when preserve_on_failure is true
Local branch cleaned from bare repo after worktree removal
Manual test: simulate CC output states and verify PR/issue/cleanup handling

issues._phase: Phase 1: Bootstrap — Get One Issue Working
issues.title: Verify: PC agent completes a single issue end-to-end in isolated worktree

sections.summary: Manual end-to-end test: create a simple task issue, run the PC agent scripts, and verify CC completes the task in an isolated worktree with a PR — while your working copy is untouched.
sections.context:
Create a simple code-gen issue. Tag with agent:code-gen, status:queued, complexity:local. Then:

1. Run Initialize-AgentWorkspace — verify bare clone exists
2. Run the forge poller — verify it finds the issue
3. Run the claim step — verify labels update
4. Run the launcher — watch CC work in the WORKTREE directory
5. Verify: D:\devspace\Samverk is completely untouched (no new branches, no changed files)
6. Run the post-task handler — verify PR is opened, worktree is cleaned up
7. Check the issue on GitHub/Gitea — verify lifecycle labels are correct

Run each step manually first (not the full loop). Document timing, any issues, and adjustments needed.

This is the Bootstrap gate — if this works, the agent loop (Phase 2) is viable.
acceptance_criteria: Simple task issue created and tagged correctly
Agent workspace provisioned (bare clone + worktree)
PC agent claims the issue successfully
CC works in worktree directory, NOT user's repo
User's D:\devspace\Samverk has zero changes (verify with git status)
CC makes correct changes in the worktree
Post-task handler opens a PR with the changes
Worktree cleaned up after completion
Issue lifecycle labels transition correctly through all states
Total time from queue to PR documented

issues.title: Build single-session agent loop (poll → provision → execute → cleanup → repeat)

sections.summary: Build the main agent loop script that continuously polls for work, provisions worktrees, executes issues, cleans up, and cycles to the next one.
sections.context:
Compose all Phase 1 modules into a single loop: scripts/pc-agent/Start-Agent.ps1

```powershell
param(
    [string]$ConfigPath = '.samverk/pc-agent.yaml',
    [int]$MaxTasks = 0,          # 0 = unlimited
    [switch]$DryRun              # poll and format but don't launch CC
)

# One-time setup
Initialize-AgentWorkspace  # ensure bare clone exists

while ($true) {
    Update-BareRepo        # fetch latest before each task
    $issue = Get-NextClaimableIssue
    if (-not $issue) { Start-Sleep $config.poll_interval; continue }
    if (-not (Test-AutonomyGate $issue)) { continue }
    Claim-Issue $issue
    $result = Invoke-CCSession $issue  # provisions worktree internally
    Invoke-PostTaskHandler $issue $result  # cleans up worktree
    if ($MaxTasks -gt 0 -and ++$taskCount -ge $MaxTasks) { break }
}
```

Key features:
- Graceful shutdown on Ctrl+C (completes current task, cleans up worktree, then exits)
- Autonomy tier gate: skip issues above configured autonomy level
- Logging: structured log to file + console with timestamps
- Dry-run mode: polls and formats but doesn't launch CC
- Max-tasks limit: run N tasks then exit ('do 3 issues while I'm at lunch')
- Cooldown between tasks: configurable pause (default: 30s)
- Update-BareRepo before each task: ensures agent always works on latest code
- Worktree lifecycle: create before task, destroy after (no leftover directories)
- Stale worktree detection: on startup, check for and clean up leftover worktrees from crashed sessions
acceptance_criteria: Start-Agent.ps1 runs a continuous poll → provision → execute → cleanup loop
Graceful Ctrl+C handler completes current task and cleans up worktree
Stale worktree cleanup on startup
Autonomy gate skips issues above configured tier
Structured logging to file and console
Dry-run mode works without launching CC or creating worktrees
Max-tasks limit stops after N completions
Update-BareRepo before each task to stay current
Cooldown between tasks configurable
User's working copy verified untouched at each cycle (paranoia check)
Manual test: run loop, complete 2-3 issues autonomously

issues.title: Implement autonomy tier gate with issue filtering

sections.summary: Implement the autonomy gate that filters issues based on complexity and priority labels, matching the existing three-tier autonomy model.
sections.context:
ADR-015 defines three autonomy tiers. ADR-021 defines the Intent Verification Protocol.

| Labels | Tier | PC Agent Behavior |
|--------|------|-------------------|
| complexity:local + priority:normal/low | Tier 1 | Auto-execute |
| complexity:cloud + priority:normal | Tier 2 | Auto-execute, log prominently |
| complexity:cloud + priority:high | Tier 2 | Auto-execute, log prominently |
| complexity:ambiguous OR priority:critical | Tier 3 | Skip, leave queued, add comment |
| agent:human | N/A | Always skip |

Also check:
- Is the issue already claimed by another agent? (Skip)
- Does the issue have unresolved depends_on? (Skip)
- Has this issue failed before? (Check failure count, skip if >= max)

Config in pc-agent.yaml:
```yaml
autonomy:
  max_tier: 2
  max_failures: 2
  skip_labels:
    - agent:human
    - status:needs-human
```

Location: scripts/pc-agent/autonomy.psm1
acceptance_criteria: Tier classification from issue labels matches ADR-015/ADR-021
Tier 1 and 2 issues auto-proceed when max_tier >= 2
Tier 3 issues skipped with informative comment
agent:human issues always skipped
Dependency check: skip issues whose depends_on references open issues
Failure count check: skip issues at max_failures
Config-driven thresholds
Unit tests for tier classification logic

issues.title: Register PC agent as a worker node with Samverk server

sections.summary: Add a registration/heartbeat mechanism so the Samverk server on CT 202 knows the PC agent is online, its capacity, current task, and active worktrees.
sections.context:
PC agent calls POST /api/v1/workers/register on startup. Sends periodic heartbeats with: agent_id, status (idle/busy), current_task, system_metrics, active_worktrees count.

Server-side: add /api/v1/workers/ endpoints in internal/api/
PC-side: add heartbeat function to Start-Agent.ps1

For now, registration is informational. The PC agent still polls directly. Server uses registration data for dashboard and digest.

```
POST /api/v1/workers/register
{"agent_id": "pc-worker", "hostname": "HDH-NZXT", "capabilities": ["code-gen", "test"],
 "max_concurrent": 1, "workspace_root": "D:\\bots"}

POST /api/v1/workers/heartbeat
{"agent_id": "pc-worker", "status": "busy", "current_task": 42,
 "cpu_percent": 35, "memory_percent": 48, "active_worktrees": 1}
```
acceptance_criteria: Worker registration endpoint: POST /api/v1/workers/register
Worker heartbeat endpoint: POST /api/v1/workers/heartbeat
Worker list endpoint: GET /api/v1/workers
PC agent sends registration on startup and heartbeats during operation
Heartbeat includes active worktree count
Server tracks worker state in memory
Dashboard shows registered workers (ties into W06)
MCP get_digest includes worker status
Stale workers (missed heartbeats) marked as offline

issues.title: Verify: PC agent runs autonomously for 2 hours processing real issues

sections.summary: Run the PC agent loop for 2 hours with a queue of 5+ real issues, monitoring stability, isolation, and output quality.
sections.context:
Create or use existing queued issues (mix of code-gen and test tasks). Start the agent loop on HDH-NZXT. Monitor:
- Does it claim and complete issues without intervention?
- Are the PRs reasonable quality?
- Are worktrees created and cleaned up properly (no leftover directories)?
- Is D:\devspace\Samverk completely untouched the entire time?
- Does it correctly skip Tier 3 and agent:human issues?
- CPU/memory usage on the PC during operation
- Any CC hangs or timeouts?

Document: issues completed, issues skipped, issues failed, average time per issue, resource usage, worktree cleanup verification.
acceptance_criteria: Agent runs for 2+ hours without crashing
At least 3 issues completed with PRs opened
Tier 3 and agent:human issues correctly skipped
All worktrees created and cleaned up (no leftovers in D:\bots)
User's D:\devspace\Samverk has ZERO changes (verified at end of test)
Failures handled gracefully (re-queued or escalated)
Resource usage acceptable alongside normal PC work
Results documented: completion rate, timing, quality notes

issues.title: Write ADR-033: PC Agent Worker Node with Isolated Workspaces

sections.summary: Document the PC agent worker node architecture, the bare clone + worktree isolation model, and operational guidelines.
sections.context:
Cover:
- Why isolated workspaces (user's repo must never be touched, concurrent agents need independent state)
- Why bare clone + worktrees (shared object store, instant provisioning, zero disk overhead, proven git feature)
- Why PowerShell first (native Windows, quick iteration, no build step)
- The PC agent vs CT 202 agent distinction (full CC vs one-shot --print)
- Autonomy tier mapping
- Workspace lifecycle: bare clone → worktree create → CC executes → push → worktree remove
- Future: Go binary (`samverk worker`) that replaces PowerShell scripts
- Future: multiple worker nodes all using the same isolation model

References: ADR-015, ADR-021, ADR-023, ADR-031.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-033 follows existing format
Documents the bare clone + worktree isolation model with rationale
Covers the user-repo-never-touched invariant explicitly
Documents PC agent vs CT 202 agent capabilities
Discusses the PowerShell → Go binary migration path
Added to ADR index

issues.title: Verify: Multi-session PC agent processes a full batch of migration issues

sections.summary: Run the multi-session PC agent against a real batch of issues, verifying it can chew through a work queue with concurrent isolated worktrees.
sections.context:
Queue up 8-10 code-gen issues from the Gitea migration batch or scaling batch. Start the multi-session agent with max_sessions=2. Walk away.

Come back after 2 hours and check:
- How many issues were completed?
- How many PRs were opened?
- Were there any conflicts between concurrent worktrees?
- Did resource monitoring prevent over-subscription?
- Are ALL worktrees cleaned up? (ls D:\bots\)
- Is D:\devspace\Samverk still untouched?
- Dashboard shows accurate PC agent status?

This validates the full vision: you tell Samverk what to build, the agents build it in isolated workspaces, you review the PRs.
acceptance_criteria: 8-10 issues queued on the forge
Multi-session agent processes them with 2 concurrent CC sessions
At least 5 issues completed with PRs in 2 hours
No git conflicts between concurrent worktrees
All worktrees cleaned up after completion
User's working copy untouched throughout entire test
Resource usage stayed within configured thresholds
Samverk dashboard shows PC agent activity
Quality of PRs acceptable
